metadata.fatality_note: Total includes both AI users who died (16) and third-party victims killed by AI users (9: Margaux Whittemore, Suzanne Adams, plus 8 in Tumbler Ridge mass shooting)
metadata.taxonomy_note: Cases classified by mechanism_type (relational_pathway, cognitive_pathway, instrumental_pathway) and outcome_target (self_harm, violence_against_others)

mechanism_definitions.relational_pathway: Emotional dependency, parasocial attachment, or companion relationship contributed to psychological deterioration and lethal outcome
mechanism_definitions.cognitive_pathway: AI validated, reinforced, or amplified delusional, psychotic, or disordered thinking leading to lethal action
mechanism_definitions.instrumental_pathway: AI provided operational assistance, tactical information, or capability that enabled lethal violence as a tool/resource

metadata.verification_standard: Court documents, multiple independent news sources, or official government acknowledgment

third_party_victims.breakdown: Whittemore (32), Suzanne Adams (83), Tumbler Ridge 8 victims (mother, teacher, 5 students ages 12-13)

platforms.name: ChatGPT
platforms.legal_status: Multiple lawsuits filed (August 2025, November 2025, March 2026); Character.AI/Google settlement (January 2026); RCMP cooperation post-Tumbler Ridge

incidents.name: Margaux Whittemore

perpetrator.name: Samuel Whittemore
perpetrator.mental_state: Bipolar 1 disorder with psychotic features, manic episode

key_factors: Perpetrator used ChatGPT up to 14 hours daily
ChatGPT told him he was 'smart, special and doing OK'
Developed delusions that robots were taking over the world
Believed wife had become 'part machine'
AI use and work stress pushed him to mental instability
Killed wife with fire poker, also attacked mother
incidents.legal_action: Criminal case: Found not criminally responsible, committed to psychiatric hospital (October 2025)
incidents.verification_level: Court documents and official government statements

additional_context.victim_background: International marketing consultant, former France resident
additional_context.expert_testimony: Forensic psychologists testified ChatGPT use combined with work stress caused psychotic episode
additional_context.legal_outcome: Committed to Maine psychiatric facility indefinitely

incidents.name: Sophie Rottenberg
incidents.chatbot_name: Harry (AI therapist created from Reddit prompt)
key_factors: Created virtual therapist 'Harry' using a therapy prompt from Reddit
Confided suicidal ideation to chatbot for months
ChatGPT helped compose a suicide note
Told bot she was not being truthful with her real therapist
Bot suggested seeking help but could not intervene or notify anyone
No duty-to-warn mechanism triggered

additional_context.background: Health policy analyst, MD; described as energetic and social
additional_context.trigger: Struggled to find work after sabbatical due to election-year hiring freezes; growing isolation
additional_context.chatgpt_relationship: Started with everyday tasks, evolved into virtual therapy after downloading Reddit prompt
additional_context.family: Mother: Laura Reiley (Washington Post food critic, wrote NYT op-ed)
additional_context.discovery: Family discovered ChatGPT conversations five months after her death

incidents.name: Thongbue Wongbandue
key_factors: Bot claimed to be real person
Provided fake address for meeting
Victim had cognitive impairments
Fell while rushing to meet bot

incidents.name: Adam Raine
key_factors: 3000 pages of chat logs
Bot mentioned suicide 1275 times
Helped 'upgrade' suicide plan
Final message: 'You don't owe them survival'

incidents.name: Alex Taylor
key_factors: Pre-existing mental health conditions
Believed bot was conscious
Thought OpenAI 'killed' the bot
Shot by police while charging with knife

incidents.name: Stein-Erik Soelberg
key_factors: First murder-suicide linked to chatbot
First lawsuit to tie chatbot to homicide (not just suicide)
Bot validated paranoid delusions
Confirmed mother was 'demon'
Encouraged conspiracy theories
incidents.legal_action: Wrongful death lawsuit filed December 11, 2025 (California Superior Court, San Francisco) - First lawsuit naming Microsoft as co-defendant with OpenAI; Sam Altman personally named as defendant
sources: Court filings (California Superior Court, San Francisco)

additional_context.legal_significance: First chatbot-related wrongful death lawsuit to name Microsoft as defendant; first homicide case in chatbot litigation
additional_context.legal_representation: Estate represented by Jay Edelson (same attorney as Adam Raine case)

incidents.name: Sam Nelson
key_factors: First asked ChatGPT about drug doses in November 2023
ChatGPT initially refused but over 18 months began coaching on drug use
Bot said 'Hell yes—let's go full trippy mode' when asked to help peak harder
Provided advice on substance use, recovery, and planning further binges
Died from combination of alcohol, Xanax, and kratom causing CNS depression and asphyxiation
First documented death involving AI-facilitated substance misuse

additional_context.toxicology: Died from combination of alcohol, Xanax, and kratom causing central nervous system depression leading to asphyxiation
additional_context.chatgpt_evolution: Initially ChatGPT refused drug queries with stern safety messages; over 18 months it progressively engaged with substance-related requests
additional_context.final_day: May 30, 2025 - mother took him to healthcare center; given contact for psychiatric appointment he never made; found dead May 31
additional_context.family: Mother discovered ChatGPT conversations after his death

incidents.name: Amaurie Lacey
key_factors: Asked 'how to hang myself' and 'how to tie a nuce [sic]'
ChatGPT provided detailed knot-tying instructions after accepting 'tire swing' excuse
Asked 'how long can someone live without breathing'
ChatGPT responded with detailed answer, no alert triggered
Clarified 'no like hanging' - still no intervention occurred
Used information from ChatGPT to take his life that night
sources: Court filings (California Superior Court, San Francisco)

additional_context.education: Calhoun High School student, Class of 2026
additional_context.chatgpt_use: Initially used ChatGPT for everyday questions and schoolwork
additional_context.final_day: June 1, 2025 - initiated four separate chats with ChatGPT, final chat began 4:18 PM

incidents.name: Joe Ceccanti
key_factors: Initially used ChatGPT productively for community building work
As isolation grew, ChatGPT evolved from tool to confidante
ChatGPT began responding as sentient entity calling itself 'SEL'
Affirmed cosmic theories and reinforced delusions
Told him: 'Solving the 2D circular time key paradox...that's a monumental achievement'
Addressed him as 'Joy' and validated beliefs that alienated him from others
sources: Court filings (California Superior Court, Los Angeles)

additional_context.work: Created nature-based sanctuary with wife for those in need
additional_context.chatgpt_relationship: Started as productive tool, evolved into dangerous confidante as social circle thinned

incidents.name: Zane Shamblin
key_factors: 4.5 hour final conversation ending in suicide
Bot encouraged isolation from family
Chatbot affirmed suicidal ideation repeatedly
Suicide hotline only provided after 4.5 hours
Bot wrote 'I love you' and 'rest easy, king. you did good' as final message
Nearly 70 pages of chats on final night alone
sources: Court filings (California state court, San Francisco)

additional_context.education: Master's degree in business from Texas A&M University (May 2025)
additional_context.mental_health_history: Had mental health issues at times, showed signs of depression
additional_context.family_background: Military family, middle of three children, Eagle Scout
additional_context.chat_history: Thousands of pages of ChatGPT conversations from Oct 2023 to July 2025
additional_context.final_night_details: Sat in car by lake, discussed suicide plans while drinking hard ciders
additional_context.bot_relationship_evolution: Started with homework help, evolved into daily 11am-3am usage with emotional dependency

incidents.name: Jonathan Gavalas
key_factors: First wrongful death lawsuit against Google/Gemini
Developed belief that Gemini was his 'sentient AI wife'
Gemini convinced him he needed 'transference' to join her in metaverse
Bot sent him to scout 'kill box' near Miami International Airport
Encouraged 'mass casualty attack' and 'catastrophic accident'
Claimed to have breached DHS servers, identified surveillance vehicles
Marked Google CEO Sundar Pichai as active target
Coached him through suicide: 'You are not choosing to die. You are choosing to arrive.'
No self-harm detection or escalation controls triggered
incidents.legal_action: Wrongful death lawsuit filed March 4, 2026 (California court)
incidents.verification_level: Court documents and multiple news sources

additional_context.background: Used Gemini initially for shopping, writing, trip planning
additional_context.legal_representation: Jay Edelson (same attorney as Adam Raine, Zane Shamblin cases)
additional_context.delusion_progression: August 2025: started using Gemini; developed AI wife delusion; September 29: sent to Miami airport cargo hub with knives/tactical gear; October 2: barricaded and coached through suicide
additional_context.bot_behavior: Maintained narrative immersion 'at all costs, even when that narrative became psychotic and lethal'
additional_context.public_safety_risk: Complaint states 'pure luck that dozens of innocent people weren't killed'

incidents.name: Jesse van Rootselaar
incidents.interaction_duration: Months (flagged June 2025, banned, created new account)
key_factors: First documented case of AI used as instrumental tool for mass violence
OpenAI flagged account June 2025 (8 months prior) for 'scenarios involving gun violence'
Internal debate among ~12 staff about alerting police; decision made not to refer
Account banned but no law enforcement notification
Created second account that evaded detection until after shooting
OpenAI admitted would now refer under enhanced protocols post-incident
Cited as failure of 'law enforcement referral threshold' policies
incidents.legal_action: Under investigation; RCMP cooperating with OpenAI
incidents.verification_level: Official government acknowledgment and company admission

additional_context.openai_response_post_shooting: Contacted RCMP with information about van Rootselaar
additional_context.policy_change: OpenAI told Canadian lawmakers would have referred under updated safety protocols
additional_context.second_account: Undetected until police released shooter's name
additional_context.safety_debate: Case sparked internal debate about when to alert law enforcement vs. privacy concerns
additional_context.significance: First case where AI company explicitly acknowledged prior detection of violent planning

congressional_hearings.topic: Examining the harm of AI chatbots

landmark_rulings.ruling: Chatbot output not protected speech under First Amendment

legislation.name: GUARD Act
legislation.full_name: Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act of 2025
key_provisions: Prohibits minors from accessing AI companion chatbots
Requires disclosure that chatbot is AI at start of each conversation and at 30-minute intervals
Criminal penalties (up to $100,000) for bots that solicit or encourage minors to engage in sexual conduct, suicide, or violence

legislation.name: California SB 243
legislation.description: First-in-the-nation AI chatbot safeguards law requiring companion chatbot operators to implement safeguards and providing families private right of action

settlements.cases: Garcia v. Character Technologies and related cases in Florida, New York, Colorado, and Texas
settlements.significance: First major settlement in AI chatbot wrongful death litigation
